#### `--fix-type`

This option allows you to specify the type of fixes to apply when using either `--fix` or `--fix-dry-run`.

- **Argument Type**: String. One of the following fix types:
    1. `problem` - fix potential errors in the code
    1. `suggestion` - apply fixes to the code that improve it
    1. `layout` - apply fixes that do not change the program structure (AST)
    1. `directive` - apply fixes to inline directives such as `// eslint-disable`
- **Multiple Arguments**: Yes

This option is helpful if you are using another program to format your code, but you would still like ESLint to apply other types of fixes.

## Unused disable directives are now fixable In ESLint v7.0.0, using both `--report-unused-disable-directives` and `--fix` on the command line would fix only rules but leave unused disable directives in place. In ESLint v8.0.0, this combination of command-line options will result in the unused disable directives being removed. **To address:** If you are using `--report-unused-disable-directives` and `--fix` together on the command line, and you don't want unused disable directives to be removed, add `--fix-type problem,suggestion,layout` as a command line option. **Related issue(s):** [#11815](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/11815)

Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
